input.quote: 6.1 Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled) and HDI shall have the exclusive right to use of the "Deerskin" brand for a self-contained web site for the offering of Deerskin Products directly to the consumer on the Internet.
input.rationale: Section 6.1 binds the Company (our party) with a non-compete/field-of-use covenant: we may not participate in any Internet project similar to the Site involving Deerskin Products or "products substantially similar" to them, including the products of unnamed "companies similar to" two named retailers, and HDI takes an exclusive right over our own "Deerskin" brand for a direct-to-consumer site. This fails the fallback on multiple material terms: the scope is not a single named competing product but an open-ended class of similar products and similar companies; there is no carve-out for our internal development or for acquisitions; and although the covenant runs "during the term", the term auto-renews annually under Section 4.1, so the restriction is not capped at 12 months. HDI's exclusive brand right also independently prevents us from using and licensing our own brand, so the preferred position cannot be met while it stands. We therefore replaced the covenant in 6.1 with a short affirmative confirmation that we are unrestricted, leaving HDI's own exclusivity covenant (6.3) and our retained closeout rights (6.2) untouched; 6.2 stands on its own, so removing the "Except as provided in Section 6.2" lead-in leaves no dangling reference.

mappings.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.

proposal.summary: Replace Section 6.1 restriction with an affirmative statement that the Company is unrestricted
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a covenant barring us from any project involving Deerskin Products or "substantially similar" products, or an exclusive right in HDI over our own "Deerskin" brand, so we have replaced Section 6.1 with confirmation that we remain free to operate and to use our brand. If HDI needs protection, we could consider a restriction limited to one named competing product, during the term only and capped at 12 months, with carve-outs for our internal development and acquisitions.
